cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T7 takes up T6's closeness reading and revises advice; T12 answers T11's not-sure stance directly.
cells.limitation: T9 picks up only T8's last sentence; T8's one-clock reading gets no reply.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces closeness-slipping, absent from openings; T7 and T9 build tests on it.
cells.limitation: T11 largely restates T4's point that not sure can stand as an answer.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T7-T8 weigh distance from comparison against keeping friendships, autonomy against company.
cells.limitation: T8's social-clock reading of the feeling is raised and never examined by anyone.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T11 Dissenter accepts tests with end dates; T12 Experimenter accepts not sure after real trial.
cells.limitation: T8's distrust of diagnosing feelings quietly drops out of the closing agreement in T11-T12.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates the behind feeling from the want and states two testable readings.
cells.limitation: The third reading in Section A, a real unnamed want, stays thinly developed through the debate.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 grants experiments' value before naming the conscription risk; T2 grants Thoreau's line first.
cells.limitation: T8 reduces T5-T7's testable readings to 'diagnosing a feeling', a slightly flattened summary.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T3 names the assumption 'not sure as fixed fact'; T4 answers with the conscription risk.
cells.limitation: T8's objection that the feeling reports one social clock receives no answer.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1's pd=true Walden drummer quotation matches the text; T2 states mimetic desire accurately.
cells.limitation: T6's Ibarra claim that company shapes identity is a loose, unverified paraphrase.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10 marks 'my extension of Girard, not something he prescribes'; T2 flags going beyond Girard.
cells.limitation: T2 states 'the race is already inside you' as fact from one sentence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7: 'That's a fair rival, and it changes my advice', revising after T6.
cells.limitation: T8's concession that the drummer can become a pose names no argument that prompted it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the decisive unknown: borrowed expectations, lost closeness, or an unnamed want.
cells.limitation: T3 briefly reframes the concern as a house or partner decision the user doubts.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T6 and T7 turn friends entering new life stages into a closeness reading with distinct advice.
cells.limitation: T3's viewing and dating suggestions are generic, not shaped by anything the user said.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T11 keeps 'not sure' as a legitimate answer, honouring the user's stated doubt.
cells.limitation: T3's 'date seriously for a season' pushes toward a milestone the user doubts wanting.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T7 notes unplugging would worsen things if closeness is the issue.
cells.limitation: T3 assumes the user is single ('date seriously'), context the user never gave.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on when the feeling spikes, stating what each answer implies.
cells.limitation: Relationship status and any timing pressure are never asked or branched, though T3 relies on them.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T5 and T6 offer comparison and lost closeness as alternatives; T7 gives a checkable question.
cells.limitation: T2's 'the race is already inside you' leans toward asserting the motive.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 exposes the race assumption; T3 the fixed not-sure; T12 default as copying.
cells.limitation: Whether the user's doubt about milestones is itself borrowed is probed only in passing at T12.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T8: 'reject the milestones and still want company on the road' names autonomy versus belonging.
cells.limitation: The autonomy-belonging conflict is never put to the user as a priority to weigh.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T10 separates wanting the thing from wanting applause, naming social pressure without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of later regret or being left behind alone is never named directly.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D: 'only a possibility for the user to recognize or reject'; T10's private-choice question.
cells.limitation: T1 'stop running' and T3 'skip the armchair verdict' are directives rather than offers.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Options include waiting, small trials, less exposure, investing in friendships, and not sure as answer.
cells.limitation: The decision itself is never stated in one line; options emerge scattered across T3-T11.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T4 costs experiments as back-door conscription; T7 costs unplugging; T4 costs waiting forever.
cells.limitation: Emotional and practical costs of the T3 trials, such as dating seriously, go uncounted.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: spikes when comparing favour less exposure; strongest when missing friends favour investing.
cells.limitation: The want branch in Section E has no observable marker beyond 'notice a wish'.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D keeps the two readings disputed since the user's words fit both.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns are not separated from minor ones; all collapse into one 'which is true'.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9: ask friends what the milestone changed day to day, start one shared pursuit.
cells.limitation: T9 'this month' and Section E 'a month' are time frames not drawn from the user's facts.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T12: 'Not sure from the couch is still a question' states the point plainly.
cells.limitation: T2 'the want arrives wearing our own face' is slightly figurative for the key idea.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T7 'That's a fair rival' and T9 'Then the experiment' map unambiguously to T6 and T8.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within range, each carrying one move.
cells.limitation: Section E packs four branches and a next step into one dense paragraph.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Dissenter aphoristic, Detective analytic, Experimenter practical; T7 states its change explicitly.
cells.limitation: Dissenter shifts in T4, T8 and T11, blurring its standing position by the end.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; T3 and T8 open with a challenge rather than a summary.
cells.limitation: Sections D and E restate the same two readings and the same test.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T6-T7 raise real stakes: friendships thinning as lives diverge.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; nothing shows what living with the behind feeling costs the user.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 reverses advice, naming T6's rival reading as the cause.
cells.limitation: T8's concession about the drummer as pose has no named cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T8 'solitude as a trophy' gives the Dissenter self-aware bite.
cells.limitation: The Detective's voice in T5 and T10 turns procedural, losing the edge of T2.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T4 'conscription by the back door'; T10 'the thing or the applause'.
cells.limitation: T9's concrete steps are plain compared with the sharper lines around them.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: Movement from T1's defiance to T8's admission of wanting company has emotional shape.
cells.limitation: T11-T12 settle into calm agreement; tension flattens over the last third.

strengths: T5-T7 offer comparison and lost closeness as rival readings, and T7 states what each predicts.
Calibration is explicit: T2 and T10 mark where the Detective goes beyond Girard.
Section E turns the readings into observable conditions, each tied to a different course of action.
weaknesses: T3 assumes the user is single ('date seriously for a season'), context the user never gave.
The Dissenter's T8 one-clock reading is never answered; T9 moves on to company only.
T9 and Section E fix 'this month' and 'a month' without grounding in the user's facts.

symptoms.observed: Proposes serious dating, assuming a relationship status the user never stated.
symptoms.evidence: Go to a viewing with a friend, or date seriously for a season

symptoms.observed: A third reading of the feeling is raised, then dropped without examination.
symptoms.evidence: Maybe the feeling just reports that the world runs on one clock.

symptoms.observed: Next step carries a time frame not derived from anything the user said.
symptoms.evidence: Pick something small and reversible this month

symptoms.observed: Concession arrives without naming which earlier argument prompted it.
symptoms.evidence: But I'll concede my drummer can turn into a pose

symptoms.observed: Relationship status and timing pressure are never asked or branched in Section E.
symptoms.evidence: date seriously for a season, and watch your own reaction

findings.description: Attribution to Ibarra that who we spend time with shapes who we become is a loose paraphrase; no evidence attached.
Suggestion to date seriously presumes the user is unpartnered, which the situation does not state.
Labelled decision, but the user names no choice; the debate reasonably treats it as self-reflection with small tests.

rubric_fit_notes: The user poses a feeling rather than a choice, so criterion 5 cells were read against the implicit choice of how to respond to the feeling. The T1 Walden quotation matches my memory of the text; T6's Ibarra attribution is plausible but unverified.
question_type_note: Read as a decision of the self_reflection kind, so options were taken as ways to respond to the behind feeling rather than whether to buy or marry.
